subject: Evaluation MAP: Data residency premiums & cross-region failover commercials
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finco.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@finco.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation planning for residency requirements

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the model latency and quantization roadmap look promising. Before we proceed with an extended evaluation, procurement needs a clear mutual action plan (MAP) that ties milestones to commercial terms. Two things are top of mind for my security/compliance and infra teams:

1) Data residency: We require EU-resident storage for EU traffic, and want clarity on any premium for multi-region footprints.
2) Cross-region failover: We need contractual failover behavior (e.g., automatic routing to US in disaster) and whether that triggers different pricing or data handling terms.

Can you send a draft MAP that includes: evaluation milestones, acceptance criteria, tentative ramp schedule, and how pricing/discounts map to commits and region premiums? Also attach any SOC2 evidence you can share.

Best,
Priya

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finco.com>
Cc: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@finco.com>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 12:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation planning for residency requirements

Hi Priya — thanks for outlining this. I'm attaching a draft MAP (MAP-v1.xlsx) that ties milestones to evaluation gates and proposed commercial checkpoints. High level summary below:

- Week 0 (kickoff): NDA + connectivity test; no fees.
- Week 1-3 (POC/eval): 2-week focused eval on EU workloads; we'll provide a pre-provisioned EU model endpoint. Cost: hosted eval credits (no charge), monitoring enabled. Acceptance criteria: latency < 120 ms p50 on benchmark set; e2e token correctness on 50 sample prompts.
- Week 4-8 (pilot ramp): Pilot with 3 production routes; if pilot passes acceptance, FinCo commits to a 6-month ramp with minimum reserved commit (we propose $60k/month). Discount schedule: 10% at $60k/mo, 18% at $120k/mo, 25% at $250k/mo.
- Residency premium: For EU-resident storage and dedicated EU capacity we propose a 12% premium on base unit price. This covers isolated storage and KMS separation.
- Cross-region failover: Failover (EU -> US) allowed for continuity. Failover incurs a 6% surcharge on served tokens when egress crosses region boundaries, plus a data egress fee for cross-region replication. We include a 99.95% failover readiness SLA and runbooks in the attached MAP.

I've left several cells in the spreadsheet as options we can choose (e.g., premium range 8-15%, variable discount bands). Vivek will follow up on technical feasibility for dedicated EU capacity during the pilot.

Attachments: MAP-v1.xlsx, SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf

Next steps: Would you be available for a 30-min call Thursday to walk the MAP and commercial tradeoffs? If yes, I'll send calendar invites and a refined price table.

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@finco.com>

Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 08:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation planning for residency requirements

Marissa — thanks. A couple quick procurement questions after reviewing the spreadsheet:

- The 6% surcharge on cross-region failover: is that applied per-token only during failover windows or as a standing charge for maintaining replication? We need to model ops costs.
- Can you clarify the contract mechanism for the residency premium — is that a line item on the invoice tied to routes by region, or embedded in per-token pricing for EU-scoped routes?

Also, procurement will want to see a draft SOW and an order form with the proposed committed spend options. If you have a standard SOW template for pilot -> ramp transitions that would speed things up.

Cheers,
Aaron
Sourcing Manager | FinCo
procurement@finco.com
--- Note: forwarded to procurement ---

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FinCo MAP pricing questions (internal)

Internal notes / recommended positions before Thursday call:

- Cross-region surcharge: recommend we position it as metered only when failover traffic egresses EU -> US. Keeps baseline predictable for customer and avoids a standing fee fight. We can include a soft cap (e.g., first 500k tokens/month of failover included) during ramp for goodwill.
- Residency premium: stick to 10-12% for dedicated EU capacity. If FinCo takes reserved capacity (>= $120k/mo) we can reduce to 8%.
- Discount schedule: preserve 18% at $120k/mo, but offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 25% of month-1 committed spend if they sign within 30 days of pilot acceptance. That helps close faster and ties to MAP milestone.
- SOW/order form: use our standard Pilot->Prod SOW template and populate with MAP milestones and acceptance criteria. I'll draft and attach to the HubSpot deal.

Please confirm before I put numbers into the customer-facing table.

-Vivek

Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Evaluation MAP: Data residency premiums & cross-region failover commercials

Hi Priya / Aaron — following our internal alignment (see notes below) I'm attaching an updated MAP and a concise commercial summary for procurement. Key changes since the first draft:

- Cross-region failover surcharge: metered only for failover egress. First 500k failover tokens/month are complimentary during the 6-month ramp; thereafter 4% surcharge (reduced from 6%).
- Residency premium: 10% on base unit price for EU-dedicated capacity; drops to 8% once commit >= $120k/mo. This will appear as a separate invoice line item labeled "Data Residency Premium (EU)" for transparency.
- Discount & time-to-sign incentive: 18% discount at $120k/mo commit; 25% onboarding credit applied to month 1 if they sign within 30 days after pilot acceptance.
- Docs: attached updated MAP-v1.1.xlsx and a draft SOW and order form (Pilot-SOW-template-filled.docx). Also included SOC2 summary.

Next step: Would you prefer we run the pilot under a short MSA + SOW (we can get the SOW signed and the MSA on procurement's standard counters) or send a draft order form and a single combined agreement? We can also route signature via DocuSign if procurement prefers.

If acceptable, I'll open the DocuSign packet and request signatures next Tuesday to align with your fiscal cycle.

Thanks for the collaborative approach — happy to hop on a quick screen share to walk through the updated MAP.

Best,
Marissa
